correctness.rationale: The signs reuse beta_k across time, so the conditional pair expectation is the Bernoulli character on the symmetric difference of two Pascal supports, not a product over independent rows. For s<t the highest differing digit produces at least 2^(popcount(t)-1) support elements absent at s. The no-increase event has probability 2^-(n-m). Fourier inversion for the fair count modulo 2^ell, ell=floor(log_2(n)/4), gives exponentially small distance to uniform in sqrt(n); Hoeffding controls fewer than ell/4 ones by exp(-ell/8). This yields the claimed power delta=1/(32 log 2) for the absolute pair bound and then the normalized bracket second moment (with the j=0 term treated separately). Along ceil(j^32) the squared estimates are summable because 32 delta>1; bounded increments interpolate, and Fubini gives the almost-sure quenched limit. The bounded martingale differences and local uniform bracket convergence then give the quenched FCLT. The finite checks in verify_pascal.py were inspected, not run, and are not a substitute for these steps.
